request.spec:
A steward can move a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claim to another person on the sheet (a refusal shows an
error on the claim). The claim keeps its number and date, loses any figure a statement bound it to
(it is live again until its new person's next statement), every total follows, and CLAIM_REASSIGNED
is written, naming the claim like every claim line (with the new person) and ending from=<old name>
to=<new name>. A settled or voided claim cannot move. The moved claim is listed as its new person's
newest claim (first under them), whatever its date.

You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can move a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claim to another person on the sheet (a refusal shows an
error on the claim). The claim keeps its number and date, loses any figure a statement bound it to
(it is live again until its new person's next statement), every total follows, and CLAIM_REASSIGNED
is written, naming the claim like every claim line (with the new person) and ending from=<old name>
to=<new name>. A settled or voided claim cannot move. The moved claim is listed as its new person's
newest claim (first under them), whatever its date.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A steward can now move a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claim to another person on the sheet. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests: the main reassign test and the three scenarios.

**How it behaves**
- Each claim row has a "Move to…" person picker and a **Move** button. Anything refused shows `claim-error` on that claim. Refusals are: the user isn't a steward, the claim is SETTLED or VOID, the person isn't on the sheet, or the claim already belongs to that person. A refusal writes nothing.
- A moved claim keeps its number and date. It loses any figure a statement bound it to, so it's live again at its new person's rate. Every total follows.
- The audit gets `CLAIM_REASSIGNED … person=<new> amount=… date=… [number=…] from=<old> to=<new>`, followed by the usual `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS` lines when figures change.
- The moved claim is listed first under its new person, whatever its date.

**What changed**
- **Listing order:** this is the only change to existing behaviour. Claims used to be listed newest first by id, which a move can't change. Migration `V27__claim_listed.sql` adds a `listed` position to each claim, numbered by a per-sheet counter. A claim gets the next number when it's made and again when it's moved, and lists now sort by that. Existing claims start with their id as their position, so their order doesn't change.
- **Server:** a new endpoint `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/reassign`, which takes `{ personId }`. It's built like the existing approve and reject endpoints. The new classes are `ValidateReassign`, `ReassignClaim`, `AuditClaimReassigned` and two small records. `Claim` gets a `reassign()` method.
- **Front end:** the picker and button are in `features/claims/claims.slot.tsx`.

**Choices the request didn't cover**
- I applied the same closed-period check the other claim actions use, so a claim dated inside a closed period can't be moved.
- I didn't block moving a claim to a retired person.
- I didn't build bulk reassign. `e2e/support/ui.ts` has a helper for it, but this spec doesn't use it.
